title: SPARK: An Efficient Hybrid Acceleration Architecture with Run-Time Sparsity-Aware Scheduling for TinyML Learning
problem: Most TinyML devices only support inference due to high hardware resource requirements for training. Enabling efficient on-device training on resource-constrained edge devices requires new acceleration approaches.
motivation: On-device training enables adaptive learning and personalization on TinyML edge devices, expanding capabilities beyond inference-only inference.
method: SPARK uses two acceleration units that work together: one standalone accelerator and another integrated directly into the CPU pipeline, allowing forward and backward propagation (the two computation passes needed for training) to run at the same time. A scheduler monitors where the computation is sparse (where many values are zero) and dynamically directs more work to whichever accelerator is free, keeping both units busy. To reduce memory bottlenecks, the system uses a shared memory architecture where data can be fetched in different orientations to match what each computation needs.
key_novelty: SPARK combines an acceleration unit built into the CPU pipeline with a scheduler that watches for sparse computation patterns in real-time to route workloads efficiently and enable simultaneous forward and backward propagation.
contributions: Hybrid acceleration architecture combining standalone and in-pipeline acceleration units
Sparsity-aware acceleration scheduler for dynamic workload distribution
Unified memory system with transposable data fetch
Achieves 4.1× performance improvement over baseline with minimal 2.27% area overhead

metrics.speedup: 4.1× vs baseline accelerator; 9.4× vs off-shelf edge devices
metrics.efficiency: 446.0× higher energy efficiency vs off-shelf edge devices

limitations: Specific limitations not discussed in abstract; generalization to other ML model types beyond TinyML not addressed.
primary_theme: Efficient TinyML training through hybrid acceleration and sparsity-aware scheduling
